name: MilkRun
failure_reason: Unsustainable Unit Economics
lesson: Sydney's quick-commerce darling raised AUD$75M+ then collapsed inside 18 months when capital tightened. Australian density couldn't support 10-minute grocery economics.

name: Send
failure_reason: Quick-Commerce Collapse
lesson: Smaller Australian quick-commerce competitor that collapsed before MilkRun, signaling the entire category's unviability locally.

name: Metigy
failure_reason: Cash Burn & Founder Issues
lesson: Sydney AI-marketing platform raised AUD$28M then collapsed amid allegations the founder used company funds for personal property. A governance failure case study.

name: Volt Bank
failure_reason: Could Not Raise Series F
lesson: Australia's first neobank to receive a banking licence handed it back in 2022 after failing to raise the AUD$200M needed to become profitable.

name: Brighte (Down Round)
failure_reason: Rates & BNPL Reckoning
lesson: Australia's solar-financing BNPL hit the same wall as global BNPL: rising rates, rising defaults, no path to profitability at peak valuation.

name: Plenti (Stock Collapse)
failure_reason: Margin Compression & Equity Collapse
lesson: ASX-listed Plenti's stock fell over 80% as Australian P2P lending margins evaporated under the rate cycle.

name: Olive AI
failure_reason: Overpromised RPA as 'AI', under-delivered ROI to hospitals
lesson: Selling AI to hospitals requires proven ROI per workflow, not a $4B narrative. Olive's automation broke on messy edge cases and clients cancelled.

name: Arrival
failure_reason: Microfactory model never produced vehicles at scale
lesson: 'Microfactories' sound capital-light in a pitch deck. In reality auto manufacturing rewards scale, and Arrival never built one.

name: Iron Ox
failure_reason: Robotic greenhouse capex could not beat commodity produce prices
lesson: Robotics + agriculture forces you to compete on lettuce price. Automation gains rarely offset the extra capital cost of the greenhouse.

name: Veev
failure_reason: Modular home factory economics broke as housing demand cooled
lesson: Modular housing has killed serial unicorns — Katerra, Veev — because factory throughput doesn't beat conventional builders once demand drops.

name: Electric Last Mile Solutions
failure_reason: SEC probe, founder exits, and unable to raise more capital
lesson: Post-SPAC EV plays with unresolved SEC issues can't raise follow-on capital. ELMS ran out of runway in 18 months.

name: Hopin
failure_reason: Pandemic tailwind evaporated overnight, valuation cratered
lesson: A pandemic tailwind is not a durable market. Hopin raised at $7.75B in a category that shrank 80% once offices reopened.

name: Thrasio
failure_reason: Bought Amazon brands at 2021 multiples, couldn't service debt
lesson: Aggregators paid 5x EBITDA for FBA brands in 2021. When Amazon fees rose and ad costs doubled, the debt stack sank them all.

name: Perch
failure_reason: Aggregator model collapsed, sold to Razor Group in distress
lesson: Perch was the 'quality' Amazon roll-up. When rates rose, quality didn't matter — every aggregator got repriced together.

name: Frank (JPMorgan)
failure_reason: Founder Charlie Javice convicted of $175M JPMorgan sale fraud
lesson: The most spectacular startup failures aren't insolvencies — they're founder-driven fraud that unwinds a nine-figure acquisition.

name: Purplebricks
failure_reason: Flat-fee model couldn't cover marketing spend as UK market cooled
lesson: In real estate, £1,000-flat-fee revenue can't fund £70M TV campaigns — the LTV/CAC math breaks the moment listings slow.

name: Shift Technologies
failure_reason: Used-car e-commerce economics broke, merger with CarLotz failed
lesson: Consolidating two failing used-car startups doesn't create a winning one — it doubles operational drag.

name: Reali
failure_reason: Cash-offer / power-buyer model unworkable as rates spiked
lesson: Power-buyer models depend on cheap capital and stable prices. When mortgage rates doubled in 2022, every buy-before-sell player broke.

name: Enjoy Technology
failure_reason: Home-visit retail model unprofitable, Apple contract insufficient
lesson: Ex-Apple retail chief Ron Johnson learned twice (JCPenney, Enjoy) that reinventing retail from famous credentials still requires unit economics.

name: Vice Media
failure_reason: Once valued at $5.7B, filed Chapter 11 in 2023 and shuttered flagship site in 2024
lesson: A cool brand, a $5.7B valuation, and a TV network still can't survive if programmatic ads and Facebook traffic evaporate together.

name: Volta Charging
failure_reason: Ad-subsidized charging model unproven, sold to Shell for $169M
lesson: 'Free' charging paid by ad impressions on the station screen was a beautiful pitch. It never actually paid for the electrons.

name: Divvy Homes
failure_reason: Rent-to-own economics broken by rates; sold to Brookfield at half valuation
lesson: Even the 'right' rent-to-own model at $2B valuation had to sell to Brookfield for half that. Housing beta ate the alpha.

name: Rally (Rally Rd)
failure_reason: Fractional collectibles secondary market never had liquidity
lesson: Fractional collectibles work as a marketing gimmick, not as a liquid secondary market. Every player in the category has stalled.

name: Argo Blockchain (US Mining ops)
failure_reason: Sold flagship Helios Texas facility to Galaxy Digital to avoid Chapter 11
lesson: Bitcoin mining is a leveraged bet on hashprice. When BTC halved and energy prices doubled in 2022, over-levered miners had to sell flagship assets to survive.

name: Core Scientific
failure_reason: BTC crash + Celsius exposure forced Chapter 11
lesson: Public miners that lent hashrate to Celsius discovered the counter-party risk when Celsius defaulted mid-2022. The debt stack did the rest.

name: Olist (Down Round & Layoffs)
failure_reason: Macro Reversal & Profitability Push
lesson: Brazil's 2021 unicorns face a brutal 2023-24 reality: SoftBank-funded growth collapsed when capital tightened and Olist-style marketplaces had to cut deep.

name: Facily
failure_reason: Unsustainable Unit Economics
lesson: Brazil's answer to Pinduoduo couldn't replicate the Chinese model's logistics density. Group-buying with subsidies burned $300M before shutdown.

name: Kavak (Brazil Exit)
failure_reason: Capital-Intensive Inventory Model
lesson: Even with $1.5B raised, Kavak couldn't make Brazilian used-car economics work and exited the country in 2023.

name: Buggy
failure_reason: Unviable Inventory Economics
lesson: A smaller used-car play that ran into the same inventory wall as Kavak — but with one-tenth the cushion.

name: Yellow (Grow Mobility)
failure_reason: Unit Economics & COVID
lesson: Brazil's biggest bike-and-scooter sharing startup couldn't reach unit economics, then COVID sealed its fate.

name: Easynvest (Sold at Discount)
failure_reason: Outcompeted by XP & Nubank
lesson: Easynvest pioneered Brazilian discount brokerage but was outscaled by XP Inc and folded into Nubank at a price below its 2018 mark.

name: Wealthsimple (Down Round)
failure_reason: Crypto Winter & Margin Compression
lesson: Canada's flagship fintech raised at CAD$5B in 2021, then accepted a CAD$1.5B mark in 2023 — destroying CAD$3.5B+ in paper value.

name: Tehama (Wind-Down)
failure_reason: Post-COVID Demand Collapse
lesson: Ottawa-based virtual-desktop startup Tehama was a COVID darling that couldn't sustain growth as remote-work tooling consolidated.

name: Thinkific (Stock Collapse)
failure_reason: Post-COVID Demand Decline
lesson: Vancouver-based Thinkific listed on the TSX in 2021 then lost over 90% of its market cap as creator-economy spending collapsed.

name: Mt. Gox
failure_reason: Hack & Mismanagement
lesson: Handling other people's money requires enterprise-grade security and compliance, not hobbyist infrastructure. Mt. Gox proved that being first-to-market means nothing if you can't protect customer assets.

name: BitConnect
failure_reason: Ponzi Scheme
lesson: Guaranteed returns in volatile markets are the hallmark of fraud. BitConnect's promised 1% daily returns were mathematically impossible and classic Ponzi mechanics.

name: QuadrigaCX
failure_reason: Fraud & Mysterious Death of Founder
lesson: Single points of failure — especially a single person controlling all private keys — create existential risk. QuadrigaCX showed that 'key man risk' can be literal.

name: Wirecard
failure_reason: Massive Accounting Fraud
lesson: Even DAX-30 companies with Big Four auditors can be complete frauds. Wirecard proved that regulatory capture and national pride can blind everyone to obvious red flags.

name: N26 US
failure_reason: Regulatory Failures & Market Misfit
lesson: European fintech success doesn't automatically translate to the US market. N26's failure in America shows that regulatory environments, competitive landscapes, and customer expectations differ dramatically.

name: Health IQ
failure_reason: Fraud — Fabricated Metrics & False Claims
lesson: Insurance is a heavily regulated industry where fabricated data doesn't just mislead investors — it violates insurance regulations. Health IQ's founder couldn't fake actuarial science.

name: Vicarious
failure_reason: Over-ambition & No Product-Market Fit
lesson: Having the most famous investors in the world cannot compensate for failing to ship a product. Vicarious spent 12 years chasing artificial general intelligence without finding a commercial application.

name: HQ Trivia
failure_reason: Founder Death, No Revenue Model & User Decline
lesson: A viral moment isn't a business model. HQ Trivia captured lightning in a bottle but never figured out how to monetize it, and the death of its co-founder accelerated a spiral that was already underway.

name: Ozy Media
failure_reason: Fabricated Metrics & Fraud
lesson: In media, inflated metrics are easy to fabricate and hard to verify. Ozy's CEO impersonated a YouTube executive on a Goldman Sachs due diligence call — the moment fraud crossed from deception into delusion.

name: Frank (JPMorgan Fraud)
failure_reason: Fabricated User Data — $175M Acquisition Fraud
lesson: When JPMorgan Chase — the largest bank in the world — can be defrauded by a startup founder who fabricated 4 million fake users, it proves that acquisition due diligence failures exist at every level.

name: Rethink Robotics
failure_reason: Over-engineering & Market Mismatch
lesson: Collaborative robots are a brilliant concept, but Rethink's Baxter was too slow and imprecise for manufacturing, and too expensive for its target market of small manufacturers.

name: Faraday Future
failure_reason: Founder Fraud, Governance Failures & Endless Delays
lesson: Faraday Future is what happens when a founder wanted by Chinese authorities for fraud convinces American investors to fund a car company that barely produces any cars.

name: DataRobot
failure_reason: Commoditization & Failed Enterprise Pivot
lesson: AutoML was a brilliant concept when data science was scarce. But as AI tools became ubiquitous and cloud providers offered their own AutoML, DataRobot's $6.3B valuation evaporated.

name: Clarifai
failure_reason: Commoditization by Cloud AI APIs
lesson: Clarifai built world-class computer vision when it was novel. Then Google, Amazon, and Microsoft offered the same thing as a $1-per-1000-images API call, destroying the premium market.

name: Mighty AI
failure_reason: Race to Bottom in Training Data
lesson: Training data labeling was critical for AI development but became a commodity service where price — not quality — won contracts. Mighty AI built a premium product in a market racing to the bottom.

name: Narrative Science
failure_reason: Niche Market & GPT Disruption
lesson: Narrative Science spent 12 years building proprietary NLG technology. Then GPT made natural language generation a commodity capability anyone could access through an API.

name: Anodot
failure_reason: Niche Market & Cloud Platform Competition
lesson: AI anomaly detection is a valuable feature but not a company-defining product. Anodot built impressive technology that cloud monitoring platforms absorbed as just another capability.

name: Determined AI
failure_reason: Open-Source Competition & Cloud Platform Bundling
lesson: ML training infrastructure was a crowded space where cloud platforms and open-source tools squeezed out standalone vendors. Even Google Ventures and Sequoia couldn't save a product without a moat.

name: Clover Health
failure_reason: SPAC Fraud Allegations & Unsustainable Losses
lesson: Chamath Palihapitiya's SPAC empire promised to democratize investing. Clover Health proved it mostly democratized losses — the stock dropped 95% while short sellers exposed undisclosed DOJ investigations.

name: Nurx
failure_reason: Regulatory Issues & Unsustainable Unit Economics
lesson: Telehealth for birth control prescriptions seemed like a perfect digital health use case. But pharmacy fulfillment costs, regulatory complexity, and insurance billing challenges made every prescription unprofitable.

name: Practice Fusion
failure_reason: DOJ Kickback Fraud & Failed Business Model
lesson: Free EHR software monetized by pharmaceutical advertising created a fatal conflict of interest. Practice Fusion's CEO went to prison for taking pharma kickbacks that influenced prescribing decisions.

name: Domo
failure_reason: Overfunding, Slow Growth & BI Market Shift
lesson: Domo raised nearly $700M to build a BI platform and still couldn't compete with Tableau, Looker, or Power BI. Sometimes the most well-funded company in a category still loses.

name: Fastly
failure_reason: Customer Concentration, TikTok Dependency & CDN Commoditization
lesson: Fastly was the 'developer-friendly CDN' that rode TikTok's growth to a $10B market cap. When TikTok optimized its CDN spend, Fastly lost its largest customer and 85% of its stock value.

name: Apttus
failure_reason: Overfunding, Complex Product & CRM Platform Dependency
lesson: Apttus raised $400M+ to build a Configure-Price-Quote platform that lived on top of Salesforce. When Salesforce built its own CPQ, Apttus lost its biggest distribution channel and its strategic moat.

name: Radius Intelligence
failure_reason: B2B Data Became Commoditized
lesson: Radius built a B2B data platform for sales intelligence. But ZoomInfo, LinkedIn Sales Navigator, and dozens of competitors commoditized B2B data, making Radius's standalone data product uncompetitive.

name: Glossier
failure_reason: DTC Model Collapse & Retail Pivot Too Late
lesson: DTC-only brands face existential risk when customer acquisition costs rise and wholesale channels are ignored too long.

name: Casper (Post-IPO)
failure_reason: Unsustainable Unit Economics & Commoditized Product
lesson: Venture-scaling a commodity product with thin margins and high return rates creates a race to the bottom that no amount of branding can win.

name: Allbirds (Post-IPO)
failure_reason: DTC Shoe Brand Failed to Scale Beyond Niche
lesson: Sustainability-focused DTC brands face brutal economics when they can't expand beyond their initial audience and face competition from incumbent brands adopting similar messaging.

name: Jet.com
failure_reason: Failed Amazon Challenger Absorbed & Shut Down
lesson: Even $3.3B acquisitions can't save a business model that can't differentiate from the dominant marketplace.

name: Farmstead
failure_reason: Online Grocery Margins Too Thin to Build Standalone Business
lesson: Online grocery delivery has the thinnest margins in e-commerce — even well-run startups can't compete with incumbents' existing infrastructure.

name: Deliveroo
failure_reason: Chronic Unprofitability Despite Massive Scale
lesson: Even with $1.7B in funding and Amazon's backing, food delivery platforms struggle to achieve sustainable profitability due to structural margin challenges.

name: Getaround
failure_reason: Peer-to-Peer Car Sharing Never Achieved Profitability
lesson: Peer-to-peer car sharing has structural challenges — supply quality is inconsistent, utilization rates are low, and the model can't compete with professional fleet operators on reliability.

name: Zum
failure_reason: School Transportation Tech Faced Razor-Thin Public Sector Margins
lesson: Modernizing public sector services (school buses) sounds transformative but faces procurement bureaucracy, budget constraints, and razor-thin margins that don't support venture returns.

name: Clubhouse (Social Audio)
failure_reason: Audio-Only Social Network Was a Pandemic Fad
lesson: Products that thrive in pandemic lockdown conditions may have zero product-market fit in the real world where people have alternatives to sitting in audio rooms.

name: SolarCity (Tesla Acquisition)
failure_reason: Unsustainable economics & bailout acquisition
lesson: Customer acquisition costs exceeded lifetime value in residential solar, requiring Tesla bailout that destroyed $2B+ in shareholder value.

name: Bloom Energy
failure_reason: Chronic unprofitability & accounting issues
lesson: Two decades of losses despite $1.7B in funding proved that fuel cell technology couldn't achieve cost competitiveness with cheaper alternatives.

name: SunEdison
failure_reason: Massive debt-fueled acquisition spree
lesson: The largest renewable energy bankruptcy in history ($16.1B in debts) was caused by reckless acquisitions financed with unsustainable debt structures.

name: Quanergy Systems
failure_reason: Failed to deliver solid-state LiDAR
lesson: Promised revolutionary solid-state LiDAR at $100/unit but never delivered a competitive product as the market was flooded with cheaper alternatives.

name: Desktop Metal
failure_reason: Revenue never matched valuation
lesson: Despite $800M raised and a $6.3B peak valuation, Desktop Metal never achieved profitability in metal 3D printing as adoption remained niche.

name: Rethink Robotics (Detailed)
failure_reason: Product didn't meet industrial needs
lesson: Pioneer of collaborative robots failed because Baxter was too slow and imprecise for real manufacturing, while cheaper and better alternatives emerged.

name: Starship Technologies
failure_reason: Unit economics didn't scale
lesson: Sidewalk delivery robots were a technical marvel but couldn't achieve cost-effectiveness versus human delivery at scale outside of campus environments.

name: SoFi Technologies
failure_reason: Student loan moratorium & competition
lesson: SoFi's core student loan refinancing business was destroyed by the federal student loan moratorium while its pivot to becoming a full bank faced intense competition.

name: Luma (Camera Hardware)
failure_reason: Smart home camera in overcrowded market
lesson: Attempted to build premium smart home camera competing against Amazon, Google, and Netgear with insufficient scale and brand recognition.

name: Velodyne Lidar
failure_reason: Pioneer overtaken by cheaper competitors
lesson: The company that invented modern LiDAR for autonomous vehicles was overtaken by cheaper competitors and sold for just $4.40/share after peaking at $24.

name: Karma Automotive
failure_reason: Luxury EV with no market
lesson: The successor to Fisker Automotive burned through $1B+ trying to sell luxury plug-in hybrids that nobody wanted, producing fewer than 3,000 cars in a decade.

name: Body Labs
failure_reason: B2B 3D body scanning market too small
lesson: Pioneering 3D body scanning technology from Brown University couldn't find enough paying customers in fashion/fitness to sustain operations.

name: Carbon Robotics
failure_reason: Hardware costs exceeded farmer ROI
lesson: AI-powered laser weeding robots were technically impressive but too expensive for most farmers, with each unit costing $1M+ and requiring specialized operation.

name: ecobee
failure_reason: Couldn't compete with Google/Amazon smart home
lesson: Canadian smart thermostat pioneer raised $200M but couldn't compete against Nest (Google) and Amazon in the smart home ecosystem war.

name: Impossible Aerospace
failure_reason: Battery-centric drone design couldn't compete
lesson: Ex-Tesla engineer's 'flying battery' drone concept couldn't achieve price-performance parity with established drone makers DJI and Skydio.

name: Essential Products (Detailed)
failure_reason: Android founder couldn't compete with Apple/Samsung
lesson: Even Andy Rubin (Android creator) couldn't build a competitive smartphone brand, as the Essential Phone sold fewer than 150K units despite massive hype.

name: Zume Pizza (Detailed)
failure_reason: Robot pizza was a solution looking for a problem
lesson: SoftBank poured $375M into robot-made pizza, then the company pivoted to compostable packaging before collapsing — a textbook case of technology in search of a market.

name: ICON (3D-Printed Homes)
failure_reason: 3D-printed homes not cheaper than traditional
lesson: Despite $451M raised and massive media hype, 3D-printed homes couldn't achieve cost savings over traditional construction when factoring in land, permits, plumbing, and electrical.

name: Peloton (Detailed Decline)
failure_reason: COVID boom was temporary, not permanent
lesson: Peloton mistook pandemic-driven demand for permanent market shift, expanded manufacturing capacity just as gyms reopened and demand collapsed 80%.

name: Getaway House
failure_reason: Overexpansion & thin margins in cabin rental
lesson: Getaway expanded to 15+ outposts chasing growth but discovered that building and maintaining remote cabins had razor-thin margins that couldn't support venture-scale returns.

name: Sonder Holdings
failure_reason: Cash burn & unsustainable lease commitments
lesson: Sonder leased apartments and operated them as hotels, but the model required massive upfront investment in each unit while generating hotel-like margins — the worst of both worlds.

name: Kiwi.com
failure_reason: Virtual interlining model collapse & airline pushback
lesson: Kiwi.com's innovation of combining flights from different airlines fell apart when airlines blocked screen scraping and refused to honor connecting itineraries they didn't sell.

name: Flyr
failure_reason: Overambitious airline SaaS pivot & cash burn
lesson: Flyr pivoted from consumer fare prediction to enterprise airline revenue management SaaS, but the sales cycles were 18-24 months and airline customers were notoriously slow adopters.

name: Notarize
failure_reason: Post-COVID demand collapse & regulatory fragmentation
lesson: Notarize exploded during COVID when remote notarization became essential, but demand collapsed as in-person services resumed and state-by-state regulations limited growth.

name: wefox (Detailed)
failure_reason: Governance scandals & unsustainable growth at any cost
lesson: Europe's most-funded insurtech raised $1.6B but faced allegations of inflated metrics, governance failures, and loss ratios that proved the business was buying revenue at unsustainable costs.

name: Vine (Detailed)
failure_reason: Twitter neglect & Instagram/Snapchat competition
lesson: Vine invented short-form video but Twitter failed to invest in creator monetization, allowing Instagram and Snapchat to poach Vine's top creators by offering money and better tools.

name: Friendster
failure_reason: Technical failures & Facebook competition
lesson: Friendster was the original social network but suffered from chronic site performance issues (20+ second load times) that drove users to MySpace and then Facebook.

name: Ello
failure_reason: No business model beyond anti-advertising manifesto
lesson: Ello attracted millions of users who hated Facebook's ads, but discovered that an ad-free social network with no subscription revenue has no way to sustain itself.

name: Path
failure_reason: 150-friend limit & failed monetization
lesson: Path's intentional 150-friend cap created intimate social sharing but severely limited growth potential and network effects, making it impossible to compete with Facebook's expanding ecosystem.

name: Google+
failure_reason: Forced adoption & no differentiation from Facebook
lesson: Even Google's massive resources and distribution (forcing G+ onto YouTube, Gmail, Android) couldn't create a social network that users actually wanted to use.

name: Mastodon
failure_reason: Complexity barrier & post-Twitter hype collapse
lesson: Mastodon's decentralized architecture appealed to idealists but confused mainstream users. Server selection, federation rules, and content fragmentation created friction that prevented mass adoption.

name: Honest Policy / PolicyGenius Struggles
failure_reason: Insurance comparison margins too thin for VC returns
lesson: Insurance comparison platforms generate leads but can't capture enough value in the transaction. Insurers pay $20-50 per lead while it costs $100+ in digital advertising to acquire each shopper.

name: Take Eat Easy
failure_reason: Brussels-founded (later Paris-headquartered) food-delivery startup Take Eat Easy, launched in 2012 by siblings Adrien and Chloé Roose with Karim Slaoui, ceased trading on 26 Jul 2016 — the same week it announced its 1-millionth delivery. After raising €16M and expanding to Paris, London, Madrid and Berlin, Take Eat Easy failed to close a Series C round it needed to compete with Deliveroo and UberEats, and filed for juridical reorganisation. It was one of the first high-profile 2010s food-delivery casualties in Europe.
lesson: Belgian-French food-delivery pioneer ran out of cash before reaching scale. The Series B that didn't close became one of Europe's most-cited startup failure post-mortems.

name: Cityscoot (Insolvency)
failure_reason: Paris-based free-floating electric scooter service Cityscoot, founded 2014 by Bertrand Fleurose, raised €70M+ from RATP, Allianz and BPI France to run one of Europe's largest shared-moped fleets. After the free-floating micromobility crash of 2022-23, Cityscoot entered insolvency proceedings at the Paris commercial court. On 21 Feb 2024 the court accepted Spanish competitor Cooltra's takeover bid for just €400k — retaining only 30 of 157-168 employees and effectively wiping shareholders.
lesson: Paris electric-scooter-sharing pioneer Cityscoot raised €60M from RATP and Allianz then filed for liquidation in 2024 — France's defining shared-mobility failure.

name: Luko
failure_reason: Paris-based home-insurance startup Luko, founded 2016 by Raphaël Vullierme and Benoît Bourdel, raised €65M and was valued at €250M in late 2020. After failing to reach profitability, Luko announced an acquisition by UK insurer Admiral in Oct 2023 for €14M — a deal Admiral pulled after audits in Nov 2023. Luko was placed in receivership in Dec 2023 and finally acquired by Allianz Direct on 25 Jan 2024 for just €4.3M (~$4.65M) at the Paris commercial court, wiping out shareholders.
lesson: Paris home-insurance unicorn-aspirant Luko was acquired by Allianz Direct subsidiary Admiral in 2023 at a steep discount, then its German subsidiary entered insolvency.

name: Habx (Acquired in Distress)
failure_reason: French Property Market Collapse
lesson: Paris PropTech Habx raised €40M to digitalize new-build property pre-sales then filed for insolvency in 2024 as the French property market collapsed.

name: Ÿnsect
failure_reason: French insect-protein pioneer Ÿnsect (founded 2011) raised over €600M — the largest agtech funding round outside the US — to build the world's largest vertical insect farm at Amiens for pet food and aquaculture feed. The Amiens facility ran years behind schedule with severe cost overruns. In Jul 2025 Ÿnsect took an €8.6M emergency bridge from historical investors alongside mass layoffs. A commercial court placed the company in supervised restructuring and extended the observation period to 12 Jan 2026. TechCrunch's Dec 2025 investigation described 'how reality crushed Ÿnsect'.
lesson: France's most-funded AgTech, insect-protein producer Ÿnsect, raised $625M then entered French safeguard proceedings in 2024 as capital-intensive scaling proved unviable.

name: ManoMano (Massive Down Round)
failure_reason: Post-COVID Demand & Profitability Push
lesson: Paris DIY-marketplace unicorn ManoMano raised $725M then conducted multiple rounds of layoffs and reportedly accepted a steep down-round in 2024 as post-COVID DIY demand collapsed.

name: Sono Motors
failure_reason: Munich-based Sono Motors listed on NASDAQ in Nov 2021 promising the Sion — a €25,000 partly solar-powered EV backed by 21,000+ pre-orders. On Feb 24 2023 the company cancelled the Sion program and laid off ~75% of staff, pivoting to a B2B solar-integration business. On May 15 2023 Sono Group NV and Sono Motors GmbH filed for self-administration (Eigenverwaltung) under the German Insolvency Act after failing to secure the ~$100M needed to bring the Sion to production.
lesson: Munich-based solar-powered car startup Sono Motors raised hundreds of millions including a Nasdaq IPO, but cancelled its consumer Sion vehicle in early 2023 and filed for insolvency three months later.

name: Auxmoney (Down Round)
failure_reason: Rate Hikes & Default Spike
lesson: Düsseldorf-based P2P consumer-lender Auxmoney conducted layoffs and a flat-to-down round as German interest-rate hikes spiked default rates and crushed P2P-lending economics in 2022-23.

name: Coya
failure_reason: Acquisition at Steep Discount
lesson: Berlin Thiel-backed digital insurer Coya raised $70M+ and was sold to Luko in 2022 at a steep discount, then collapsed entirely with Luko's own insolvency in 2023.

name: Kiwigrid
failure_reason: Insolvency After Strategic Investor Pullback
lesson: Dresden energy-IoT startup Kiwigrid filed insolvency in 2024 after corporate strategic investors LG and E.ON pulled support — a classic German corporate-VC dependency failure.

name: VEACT
failure_reason: Customer Concentration & Insolvency
lesson: Munich automotive-CRM SaaS VEACT filed insolvency in 2023 after over-reliance on a small group of large dealer-group customers — one of the German automotive-tech failures of the year.

name: Infarm
failure_reason: Berlin-based vertical farming unicorn Infarm, founded by Israeli siblings Erez & Guy Galonska and Osnat Michaeli, raised over $500M and reached $1B+ valuation in Dec 2021. In Nov 2022 the company announced a mass restructuring, closing operations in the UK, France, Netherlands, Spain, Portugal, US and Denmark to focus on 'Growing Centers' in fewer, larger locations. Its Dutch arm was declared bankrupt in 2023, and by Dec 2023 Sifted reported Infarm had 'all but disappeared' — a textbook case of vertical-farming unit economics failing at scale.
lesson: Berlin's vertical-farming unicorn raised $600M to grow herbs in supermarkets across Europe, then exited every European market in 2023 as the energy crisis destroyed already-thin unit economics.

name: Flink (Down Round & Retreat)
failure_reason: Berlin quick-commerce startup Flink hit a $5B valuation at the peak of the 2022 speedy-grocery bubble, then watched its category collapse — Gorillas was acquired by Getir, Getir itself exited the US/UK/Europe, and Gopuff retreated. In Sep 2024 Flink raised $150M ($115M equity + $35M debt) from Mubadala, Bond, Northzone and REWE at a valuation of just under $1B — an ~80% down round. Flink is now one of Europe's last surviving speedy-grocery players but the equity story of 2021 is fully unwound.
lesson: Berlin quick-commerce challenger Flink raised $1.1B at $5B valuation, then exited France in 2023 and accepted a steep down-round in 2024 as the entire q-commerce category collapsed.

name: Snapdeal
failure_reason: Intense Competition & Cash Burn
lesson: Snapdeal was once India's #1 e-commerce platform but lost to Flipkart and Amazon India by trying to be everything at once instead of finding a defensible niche.

name: Housing.com
failure_reason: Founder Misconduct & Cash Burn
lesson: A brilliant product cannot survive a toxic founder. Rahul Yadav's public feuds with investors led to his firing and the company's decline.

name: Hike Messenger
failure_reason: WhatsApp Dominance & Constant Pivots
lesson: India's WhatsApp killer never found product-market fit despite $261M in funding. Constant pivots — messaging to social to content to crypto — signaled a lack of clear vision.

name: Koo
failure_reason: User Retention & Monetization Failure
lesson: Being the 'Indian Twitter' with government support wasn't enough. Without organic user engagement and a monetization model, Koo couldn't survive.

name: Lido Learning
failure_reason: Post-COVID Demand Collapse & Cash Burn
lesson: Lido expanded from 300 to 1,200 employees during COVID but couldn't sustain growth when schools reopened. The company shut down overnight, leaving employees without their last salary.

name: Vedantu
failure_reason: Post-COVID Demand Decline & Cash Burn
lesson: Vedantu achieved unicorn status during COVID but laid off 40% of staff in 2022. The live tutoring model was too expensive for India's price-sensitive parents.

name: ShopClues
failure_reason: Founder Disputes & Competition
lesson: ShopClues reached unicorn status targeting Tier 2-3 India but collapsed due to founder disputes and inability to compete with Flipkart/Amazon.

name: PepperTap
failure_reason: Unsustainable Unit Economics
lesson: India's hyperlocal grocery delivery economics didn't work in 2015. PepperTap spent ₹300 to deliver a ₹150 order. It was 8 years too early for quick commerce.

name: TinyOwl
failure_reason: Mismanagement & Premature Scaling
lesson: TinyOwl expanded from 1 to 11 cities, then retreated to 1. Employees held the founder hostage when layoffs were announced without severance. A cautionary tale of startup chaos.

name: Paytm Mall
failure_reason: Cashback Fraud & Strategic Confusion
lesson: Paytm Mall's O2O (online-to-offline) model confused merchants and customers. Rampant cashback fraud by sellers inflated GMV artificially.

name: BharatPe
failure_reason: Governance Crisis & Founder Scandal
lesson: BharatPe's co-founder Ashneer Grover became famous on Shark Tank India but was ousted over alleged financial fraud. The company survived but was severely damaged.

name: Zilingo
failure_reason: Accounting Fraud & Governance Failure
lesson: Zilingo's Indian-origin CEO was suspended for alleged accounting irregularities. The Sequoia-backed fashion platform was liquidated after a forensic audit revealed revenue inflation.

name: FreshMenu
failure_reason: Cloud Kitchen Economics & Competition
lesson: FreshMenu built cloud kitchens before it was trendy but couldn't compete with Swiggy and Zomato's aggregation model. Vertical integration in food delivery is capital-intensive.

name: Udaan
failure_reason: Cash Burn & B2B Marketplace Challenges
lesson: Udaan became the fastest Indian unicorn but discovered that digitizing India's fragmented B2B trade required enormous capital and patience.

name: CommonFloor
failure_reason: Competition & Market Timing
lesson: CommonFloor was acquired and shut down by Quikr. Despite innovation (3D property tours, community features), it couldn't build a sustainable business in India's fractured real estate market.

name: Rivigo
failure_reason: Capital-Intensive Model & Market Challenges
lesson: Rivigo tried to revolutionize Indian trucking with relay-based logistics but the asset-heavy model burned through $325M without achieving profitability.

name: Portea Medical
failure_reason: Unit Economics & Scaling Challenges
lesson: Home healthcare in India sounds perfect on paper but Portea discovered that managing thousands of healthcare workers across cities with razor-thin margins is incredibly difficult.

name: WhiteHat Jr
failure_reason: Misleading Marketing & Post-Acquisition Write-Down
lesson: WhiteHat Jr's aggressive marketing — featuring fake student success stories and dubious coding claims for 6-year-olds — made it a poster child for EdTech hype. Acquired by Byju's for $300M, it was later written down to near zero.

name: Dazo
failure_reason: Unit Economics & Market Timing
lesson: Dazo tried to deliver home-cooked meals from households but the model couldn't ensure quality, hygiene, or consistency at scale.

name: Unacademy
failure_reason: Excessive Acquisitions & Post-COVID Decline
lesson: Unacademy made 10 acquisitions including PrepLadder ($50M), CodeChef, and Relevel but couldn't integrate them. When EdTech demand fell, the conglomerate structure bled cash from every direction.

name: Meesho (Challenges)
failure_reason: Profitability Struggles & Model Pivots
lesson: Meesho pivoted from social commerce to zero-commission marketplace, capturing massive volumes but with razor-thin margins. Profitability remained elusive despite 150M+ transacting users.

name: Vogo
failure_reason: COVID Impact & Asset-Heavy Model
lesson: Vogo's scooter rental business was devastated by COVID. Maintaining 10,000+ scooters across cities required massive capital that dried up when shared mobility demand collapsed.

name: Stayzilla
failure_reason: Competition & Founder Arrest
lesson: Stayzilla was one of India's oldest startups. Its founder was arrested over a vendor payment dispute after shutdown — highlighting the legal risks of startup failures in India.

name: Grofers (pre-Blinkit)
failure_reason: Model Failure & Forced Pivot
lesson: Grofers' original same-day grocery delivery model failed. Only after pivoting to 10-minute delivery (Blinkit) and selling to Zomato for $568M did it find a sustainable path — but as a different company entirely.

name: Fabelio
failure_reason: Cash Burn & Failed Funding Round
lesson: Indonesia's Wayfair-style furniture e-commerce raised US$30M then declared bankruptcy in 2022 after failing to secure a Series C.

name: TaniHub
failure_reason: Pivot Fatigue & Layoffs
lesson: Indonesia's flagship AgTech raised US$110M then conducted multiple rounds of layoffs as commodity-margin AgTech proved harder than projected.

name: Pluang (Down Round)
failure_reason: Crypto Winter & Path to Profit
lesson: Indonesia's wealth-app Pluang raised US$160M during the crypto boom then conducted layoffs and reportedly accepted a flat-to-down round.

name: Ula
failure_reason: Capital-Intensive Inventory Model
lesson: Tiger-Global-and-Bezos-backed Ula raised US$140M then shut down its core B2B Indonesia operations in 2023 — a major regional B2B e-commerce failure.

name: Sirclo (Layoffs)
failure_reason: Post-COVID Demand & Profitability Push
lesson: Indonesia's Shopify-equivalent Sirclo raised US$130M then conducted significant layoffs and shut acquired brands as Indonesian e-commerce SaaS margins disappointed.

name: Halofina (Wind-Down)
failure_reason: Failed to Reach Scale
lesson: Indonesian financial-planning app Halofina shut down in 2023 — a representative example of smaller Indonesian fintech apps failing to reach scale.

name: Mosaicoon
failure_reason: Pivot Fatigue & Cash Burn
lesson: Italy's most-hyped video-content startup pivoted three times in five years and ran out of runway before finding scalable revenue.

name: Hype/Banca Sella Pivot
failure_reason: Strategic Failure & Banca Sella Buyback
lesson: Italian neobank Hype, after raising €80M+ in a JV with Illimity, was bought back by Banca Sella in 2023 at a discount as the JV failed to reach scale.

name: MoneyFarm (Flat Round & Layoffs)
failure_reason: Failed to Reach Profitability
lesson: Italian wealthtech MoneyFarm raised €170M+ then conducted layoffs and reportedly accepted a flat-to-down round in 2023 as European wealthtech profitability remained elusive.

name: Scalapay
failure_reason: Milan BNPL unicorn Scalapay raised $808.5M across 5 rounds and hit $1B valuation in Feb 2022 backed by Tencent, Tiger Global and Willoughby Capital. As the global BNPL bubble burst (Klarna's valuation fell 85%, Affirm halved), Scalapay never raised a priced up-round after 2022 and quietly shifted to debt financing — a $81.5M debt facility in Dec 2025 signalled that equity markets had closed. Layoffs and market retrenchment followed as unit economics on 'pay in 3' collapsed under rising rates and defaults.
lesson: Milan BNPL unicorn Scalapay reached $1B valuation in 2022, then suffered significant reported markdowns and layoffs as the global BNPL sector collapsed (Klarna -85%, Affirm -90%).

name: MainStreaming (Insolvency)
failure_reason: Liquidation & Asset Sale
lesson: Milan video-streaming infrastructure startup MainStreaming filed liquidation in 2024 after over a decade trying to compete with hyperscale CDNs.

name: Supplyme
failure_reason: Failed to Find PMF in Italian SMBs
lesson: Turin B2B SaaS Supplyme failed to scale Italian SMB procurement and shut down in 2023 — representative of dozens of small Italian SaaS failures of the early-2020s wave.

name: Milkman (Insolvency)
failure_reason: Last-Mile Unit Economics
lesson: Milan last-mile-delivery startup Milkman raised €30M then filed for restructuring in 2024 as Italian last-mile delivery unit economics collapsed.

name: SmileDirectClub
failure_reason: Regulatory fights, dentist opposition, unit-economics collapse post-IPO
lesson: Regulated categories don't reward 'move fast and break things'. SDC's IPO peak was $8.9B; investor dentists and 30+ state dental boards eventually broke the D2C aligner model.

name: Cue Health
failure_reason: Post-Covid demand collapse, FDA authorization issues, cash-out failure
lesson: Pandemic-boom hardware companies rarely survive normalisation. Cue's at-home molecular test was clinically excellent but had no non-Covid demand curve.

name: Plastiq
failure_reason: SPAC deal collapse, failed to reach profitability in embedded finance
lesson: SPAC merger cancellations often precede bankruptcy: they represent the last public-market signal that professional investors won't underwrite a business at claimed value.

name: Tally
failure_reason: Failed to raise follow-on round, high cost of consumer credit under rising rates
lesson: a16z-scale funding doesn't inoculate against category math: consumer-credit refinancers can't out-earn the interest rates they refinance at when their own cost of capital rises.

name: Modsy
failure_reason: Post-pandemic e-commerce home spending crash + service unit economics never worked
lesson: Marketplace + service hybrids rarely reach margin at consumer prices. Modsy's $89 room design fee never covered the human-hour cost of a 3D-rendered layout.

name: Plenty Unlimited
failure_reason: Vertical farming unit economics never worked at scale; last-ditch pivot to strawberries too late
lesson: The third $1B vertical farming failure of the decade (after AeroFarms and Infarm). LED + labour + water costs kept category unit economics permanently negative at consumer prices.

name: Flip (TikTok Rival)
failure_reason: Failed to reach TikTok-scale engagement; social commerce economics never justified $1B valuation
lesson: Direct TikTok clones with paid GMV incentives can juice topline but not creator retention. Flip's $1B valuation assumed viral organic growth that never happened.

name: Fair.com (Car Subscription)
failure_reason: SoftBank-scale funding met catastrophic unit economics on used-car depreciation
lesson: Fair burned $2.1B on the belief that a weekly car-subscription would unlock rideshare drivers. When Uber renegotiated the partnership in 2020, the volume base disappeared overnight.

name: Corinthian Colleges
failure_reason: CFPB and DOE fraud investigations; predatory lending scheme against low-income students
lesson: Business models built on federal student-loan arbitrage collapse when regulators finally act. Corinthian's students received $480M+ in federal loan discharges — the largest borrower-defense relief in US history at the time.

name: LeSports (LeEco Sports)
failure_reason: Parent company LeEco's cash crisis; over-paid sports rights collapsed
lesson: China's second-largest sports rights collapse of the 2010s. LeSports paid unsustainable prices for Premier League and NBA rights that its parent LeEco couldn't cover.

name: Digital River (SaaS Division)
failure_reason: Loss of anchor Microsoft contract; commoditisation of Merchant-of-Record services
lesson: Merchant-of-Record providers depend on 1-2 anchor clients for 30-60% of revenue. Losing Microsoft in 2023 removed Digital River's revenue base while Stripe/Paddle competed for what remained.

name: Byju's (Global Collapse)
failure_reason: Insolvency proceedings on BCCI petition; largest edtech collapse in history
lesson: Byju's collapse is the most-cited edtech unravelling in history: $6B+ raised, $22B peak valuation, insolvency triggered by a $19M cricket-board sponsorship default.

name: Dash
failure_reason: Mismanagement & Missing Funds
lesson: Ghanaian-founded, Nigeria-active payments startup Dash raised US$33M in seed (largest ever in Africa at the time) then was wound down by investors after $25M+ went unaccounted.

name: 54gene
failure_reason: Strategic Confusion & Founder Departure
lesson: Africa's most-funded genomics startup, 54gene, shut down after founder departed amid governance disputes and capital exhaustion.

name: Lazerpay
failure_reason: Failed to Raise Seed & Crypto Winter
lesson: Nigerian crypto-payments startup Lazerpay shut down after a year, a representative case of African crypto startups hit by both crypto winter and Nigerian regulatory crackdowns.

name: Thepeer
failure_reason: Slow Adoption & Failed Product-Market Fit
lesson: Lagos B2B fintech-API startup Thepeer shut down in April 2024 after failing to find sufficient adoption — a transparent founder post-mortem.

name: Doohickey AI
failure_reason: Product-market fit, rapid AI changes
lesson: Even accelerator pedigree and fresh VC capital can't save a startup that hasn't nailed product-market fit before the underlying technology landscape shifts beneath it.

name: Trela
failure_reason: Failed to close funding round; capital-intensive logistics unsustainable
lesson: Just-in-time grocery in emerging markets still eats capital faster than it generates margin — Trela's efficient model wasn't enough once Brazilian LatAm funding tightened and rivals also retreated.

name: Entropy
failure_reason: Failed to reach venture-scale growth; returning capital to investors
lesson: Even top-tier crypto funding doesn't guarantee product-market fit — a16z-backed Entropy chose to wind down and return capital rather than pivot again, illustrating discipline over survival theater.

name: Parker
failure_reason: Bankruptcy, acquisition talks failed
lesson: Over-hiring and reactive decisions can lead to financial instability, even for well-funded startups with significant revenue.

name: Prime 7 Bar & Restaurant
failure_reason: Bankruptcy filing (Chapter 11)
lesson: Even beloved, high-traffic restaurants can collapse under debt and rising costs; hospitality businesses need disciplined capital structures to survive seasonal and economic swings.

name: Dunzo
failure_reason: Mounting debt, failed competition
lesson: Even significant funding and strategic investors cannot guarantee survival against intense competition and financial mismanagement in a high-burn industry.

name: BluSmart
failure_reason: Founder fraud (SEBI probe), diverted loan funds, cash crunch
lesson: Lack of corporate governance and financial impropriety can swiftly lead to the collapse of a promising startup, regardless of its market potential.

name: Good Glamm Group
failure_reason: Cash crunch, failed refinancing, lenders forced brand-by-brand sale
lesson: A roll-up 'house of brands' only works if the parent can service debt and integrate acquisitions — when a single anchor deal fell through, Good Glamm's entire capital stack collapsed and lenders dismantled the unicorn brand by brand.

name: Otipy
failure_reason: Quick-commerce killed the model; failed to close new funding round
lesson: 10-minute delivery reset consumer expectations across Indian grocery — Otipy's next-day farm-to-fork model became structurally uncompetitive against Blinkit and Zepto no matter how efficient its logistics were.

name: Subtl.AI
failure_reason: Lack of focus, poor product-market fit
lesson: A clear, narrow market focus and a credible path to your next funding round matter as much as the technology itself — especially in crowded, fast-moving categories like generative AI.

name: Monarch Tractor
failure_reason: Hardware unit economics, failed pivot to software, dealer lawsuits
lesson: Full-stack hardware startups need a working commercial product before pivoting to software — Monarch's $100K autonomous tractors underdelivered, dealer lawsuits piled up, and the software pivot came too late to save the company.

name: Sonex Aircraft
failure_reason: Severe drop-off in sales, bank pressure
lesson: A long operating history and loyal niche customer base don't protect a manufacturer from a liquidity crisis — sustained unprofitability plus a credit pullback can force an immediate shutdown with little warning.

name: HiPhi
failure_reason: Cash crunch, failed to compete with BYD/Tesla in China EV price war
lesson: Chinese luxury EV upstarts couldn't survive the BYD-led price war — HiPhi burned through $1B+ chasing a premium positioning that collapsed the moment scaled incumbents cut prices.

name: Altigreen
failure_reason: Cash crunch, unpaid dues to vendors and employees, halted manufacturing
lesson: Being early in Indian commercial EVs isn't a moat when incumbents (Mahindra, Bajaj, Piaggio) launch competitive electric 3-wheelers with dealer networks and financing — Altigreen ran out of runway before scale.

name: ANS Commerce
failure_reason: Acquirer Flipkart wound up operations
lesson: Being acquired by a large strategic buyer doesn't guarantee long-term survival — if the underlying unit economics don't improve post-acquisition, parent companies will shut down even previously well-funded businesses.

name: Beepkart
failure_reason: Funding winter, unit economics, failed to raise follow-on
lesson: Used two-wheeler resale requires deep working capital and margin discipline — BeepKart couldn't outlast India's 2024-25 funding winter, and mass layoffs preceded a quiet asset-sale exit rather than a going-concern shutdown.

name: BharatAgri
failure_reason: Failed to close $6-8M round; funding winter for Indian agritech
lesson: Advisory-only agritech models struggle to monetize Indian farmers directly — BharatAgri couldn't reach profitability before capital dried up in an 80%-down agritech funding cycle.

name: Blip
failure_reason: Lack of capital for expansion
lesson: Applying a proven business model (like quick-commerce) to a new category doesn't guarantee success — fashion's inventory and operational complexity requires far more capital before viable unit economics.

name: CodeParrot
failure_reason: High cash burn, lack of follow-on funding
lesson: YC acceptance and a hot AI category aren't enough — startups still need disciplined burn management and a credible path to differentiated, defensible value before the funding window closes.

name: NeuroPixel.AI
failure_reason: Cash crunch
lesson: Building a genuinely innovative vertical AI product isn't enough protection — if your core capability can be replicated by general-purpose foundation models, you need a defensible moat beyond the technology itself.

name: Covrzy
failure_reason: Cash crunch
lesson: Startups with thin funding cushions are highly vulnerable to key personnel departures; when acquisition offers arrive during a cash crunch, rejecting them can foreclose the only viable exit.

name: Kiki
failure_reason: Unsustainable business economics
lesson: Persistent pivoting without achieving product-market fit, even with sufficient funding and years of runway, is a strong predictor of eventual failure — especially when core customers remain confused about the business model.

name: Ascend Elements
failure_reason: Chapter 11 amid EV demand slowdown and rollback of clean-energy incentives
lesson: Cleantech scale-ups with government-loan-and-EV-demand assumptions baked in are one policy shift away from insolvency — Ascend's $900M+ raise couldn't outrun the 2025-26 EV slowdown and Trump-era incentive rollback.

name: CaaStle
failure_reason: Alleged $300M investor fraud by CEO, Chapter 7 bankruptcy
lesson: Fabricating financials to keep raising doesn't buy time — it converts a struggling business into a criminal case and wipes out every stakeholder. CaaStle went from unicorn to Chapter 7 liquidation once auditors uncovered years of forged bank statements.

name: PosiGen
failure_reason: Chapter 11 amid high interest rates, tariff shock, TPO/ITC policy uncertainty
lesson: Even mission-aligned installers can't outrun rate shock and policy whiplash — PosiGen's LMI-focused solar leases were structurally sound but its capital stack couldn't survive 2025's cost-of-capital repricing.

name: Synapse Financial Technologies
failure_reason: Chapter 11 collapse; ~$85M in end-user deposits went missing across partner banks
lesson: BaaS middlemen created a systemic risk regulators never fully oversaw — Synapse's collapse froze 100,000+ Americans' savings and exposed the 'FDIC-insured' promise of fintech as marketing, not law.

name: Yotta Technologies
failure_reason: Deposits vanished after Synapse (BaaS provider) went bankrupt
lesson: A consumer fintech is only as trustworthy as its BaaS partner — Yotta customers followed the app's promises, not the actual bank of record, and were left with claims against a bankruptcy estate instead of insured deposits.

name: IO Biotech
failure_reason: Filed for Chapter 7 bankruptcy
lesson: A single pivotal trial narrowly missing statistical significance can be as fatal to a biotech's near-term viability as an outright failure, especially when regulators require an entirely new registrational study.

name: Lipella Pharmaceuticals
failure_reason: Bankruptcy, inability to develop drug
lesson: Positive clinical trial data does not guarantee survival; without continued access to capital markets, even scientifically promising biotechs can be forced into bankruptcy.

name: Nine Square Therapeutics
failure_reason: Liquidity crisis, funding standstill
lesson: Even well-funded platform biotechs targeting scientifically validated but historically undruggable targets can run out of runway if they cannot translate discovery into a compelling near-term catalyst.

name: Builder.ai
failure_reason: Builder.ai, a Microsoft-backed 'AI-powered' app development platform once valued at $1.5 billion, collapsed into insolvency after revelations that its 'AI' was largely human engineers and that revenue
lesson: Marketing an unproven or partially fake AI capability to inflate valuation is unsustainable — eventually revenue, technology, and reality must align, or collapse follows.

name: Northvolt
failure_reason: Northvolt, Europe's flagship EV battery champion once valued at over $10 billion, filed for bankruptcy in Sweden in March 2025 after burning through more than $15 billion in funding without reaching s
lesson: Raising enormous capital cannot substitute for proven manufacturing execution — hardware startups must de-risk production processes before scaling to gigafactory volumes.

name: 23andMe
failure_reason: Once valued at $6 billion, DNA testing pioneer 23andMe filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in March 2025 after a massive 2023 data breach, collapsing demand for one-time genetic tests, and failure to buil
lesson: Owning valuable data is not the same as owning a sustainable business model — and a single catastrophic breach of customer trust can be fatal for a company built on sensitive personal information.

name: Canoo
failure_reason: Electric vehicle startup Canoo filed for Chapter 7 bankruptcy and ceased all operations in January 2025, liquidating its assets after years of production delays, executive turnover, and chronic cash s
lesson: SPAC hype and government or corporate pilot deals cannot substitute for proven, scalable manufacturing — EV startups need capital discipline and production execution.

name: Yupp
failure_reason: Growth stalled after novelty wore off; consumer LLM-comparison thesis couldn't sustain retention
lesson: A famous cap table and a hot thesis can't rescue a consumer product with no repeat-use loop. If DAU/WAU flattens 3 months post-launch, no amount of VC can fix it.

name: Zeepay
failure_reason: Ghana central bank revoked e-money issuer licence over prolonged solvency and governance failures
lesson: In regulated fintech, your licence is your business. Missed capital ratios and governance lapses can end an entire company in a single regulator letter.

name: Gigbanc
failure_reason: Could not raise a follow-on round in a chilled Nigerian fintech funding market
lesson: Sub-$5M raised in a hard market means an 18-month runway if you are lucky. Line up the acquirer before you announce the wind-down.

name: AstrumU
failure_reason: Ran out of capital before enterprise sales cycles closed at scale
lesson: Selling to universities and enterprise HR at the same time is two 18-month sales cycles overlaid. Pick one buyer or you burn through both budgets.

name: Zeen (formerly Landing)
failure_reason: Never reached the scale required for a venture-backed consumer social business
lesson: If your app doesn't cross a million MAU after two pivots, no amount of aesthetic polish will unlock venture-scale outcomes. Return the money or sell the domain.

name: Smashing
failure_reason: Curation apps cannot compete with algorithmic feeds and AI summaries for consumer attention
lesson: 'A better feed' is not a business. Readers don't pay, ads need scale, and AI now writes the summary you built a company around.

name: Ample
failure_reason: Capital-intensive swap-station rollout outran a fleet-only revenue model
lesson: Hardware + real estate + energy is three businesses in a trench coat. If you don't have OEM co-investment or utility rate-basing, the CapEx will bury you.

name: JiviAI
failure_reason: Ran out of runway before proving clinical adoption of a medical LLM
lesson: Selling AI into regulated healthcare requires 24+ months and hospital champions. If you can't clear that milestone with 18 months of runway, don't start.

name: Miga Health
failure_reason: Virtual specialty care model couldn't clear payer reimbursement thresholds
lesson: Virtual specialty clinics live or die on payer contracts. If your CPT-code strategy isn't proven in year one, your Series A math is fiction.

name: Joon Care
failure_reason: Consolidation into larger virtual mental-health platform via acqui-hire
lesson: If the category consolidates before you find defensible unit economics, taking the acqui-hire is the responsible ending, not the failure.

name: AscendEX
failure_reason: Liquidity crisis compounded by unexplained founder silence
lesson: Custody businesses run on trust. Any founder communication gap during a liquidity event triggers a bank-run, whether or not the balance sheet supports it.

name: Talrop
failure_reason: AI-driven curriculum obsolescence and financial mismanagement
lesson: EdTech curricula that teach a skill AI now does are graveyards. If your syllabus needs a rewrite every 6 months to stay relevant, your unit economics won't survive.

name: iRobot
failure_reason: Failed Amazon acquisition + Chinese Roomba clones destroyed pricing power
lesson: A pending acquisition is not an insurance policy. Regulatory blocks kill your Plan B. If your product is a commoditized SKU, an EU antitrust ruling can end your independence.

name: Picnic
failure_reason: Food-service labor economics didn't justify $100k+ pizza-assembly robots
lesson: Automation ROI must beat minimum-wage plus benefits, in the counterfactual, not in the pitch deck. Pizza labor is $15/hr — that's a $30k/year threshold no six-figure robot beats.

name: Cartwheel Robotics
failure_reason: Ran out of capital before completing seed round for capital-intensive humanoid hardware
lesson: Humanoid robotics is a $100M seed category disguised as a $3M seed category. Don't start unless you have signed commitments from Series A leads before shipping.

name: Locus Robotics
failure_reason: Robots-as-a-Service unit economics never turned positive at scale
lesson: RaaS gross margins < hardware gross margins < software gross margins. If your Series F pitched software multiples on RaaS revenue, the Series G markdown is brutal.

name: Cushion
failure_reason: Consumer fintech unit economics couldn't scale beyond niche users
lesson: 'AI negotiates your bank fees' works as a demo. It doesn't work as a business because banks won't pay the arbitrage forever, and consumers won't pay for a service that returns their own money.

name: Ember Sword
failure_reason: Crypto game economics collapsed; virtual land holders lost value
lesson: Selling virtual land before a game is playable is fundraising, not product development. When the game doesn't ship, the SEC and the pitchforks come.

name: Battlebound
failure_reason: Blockchain-gaming category couldn't retain players between hype cycles
lesson: If your monetization requires token liquidity that requires new players that requires token liquidity, you have built a fragile flywheel that stops in month 6.

name: Ami Colé
failure_reason: D2C beauty economics collapsed under retail-competition and marketing cost inflation
lesson: Being a beloved indie brand isn't a business. If you can't defend >50% gross margin with paid CAC below $60, close before you owe suppliers.

name: Inspirna
failure_reason: Failed to raise Phase 3 funding; folded before pivotal trial
lesson: If you can't fund the Phase 3 you designed, the design was wrong. Downsize the trial or partner years earlier.

name: theGist
failure_reason: Product commoditized by native features in Slack, Google Workspace and ChatGPT
lesson: If your product summarizes Slack or Gmail, Slack and Gmail will summarize themselves within 12 months. Choose a defensible wedge or die on the platform update.

name: Dot (New Computer)
failure_reason: Consumer AI companion market couldn't sustain subscription retention
lesson: Companion apps have Tinder-like uninstall rates. If your product depends on emotional connection with a chatbot, expect 90% churn at day 30.

name: Humane
failure_reason: Product-market fit collapse; laser-projector wearable rejected by reviewers
lesson: A hardware moonshot needs a job that a phone cannot already do better. The AI Pin lost every side-by-side comparison against a smartphone.

name: Fisker Inc.
failure_reason: Manufacturing chaos, software failures, and cash burn on the Ocean SUV
lesson: Contract-manufacturing an EV without owning software integration is a recipe for recall hell. Second-time founders are not automatic proof of execution.

name: Lilium
failure_reason: Insolvency after German government refused €100M loan guarantee; ducted-fan design never certified
lesson: Betting the company on a technically ambitious design and a single government backstop is not a strategy. Certification, not renderings, is the eVTOL moat.

name: Volocopter
failure_reason: Insolvency after failing to certify VoloCity before Paris 2024 and running out of runway
lesson: "Launch at the Olympics" is a marketing plan, not a certification plan. Missing a hyped date destroyed Volocopter's ability to raise the next round.

name: Bench Accounting
failure_reason: Cash crunch and negative unit economics on bundled human bookkeeping; assets acquired by Employer.com
lesson: Human-labor SaaS looks like SaaS on the surface until you look at gross margin. Bench's margins never supported its growth spend.

name: 2U Inc.
failure_reason: Chapter 11 after Online Program Manager revenue-share model collapsed under university pushback and Dept. of Ed rules
lesson: Regulatory arbitrage is not a business model. When the US Department of Education signals it will kill your revenue share, your equity has already been destroyed.

name: Invitae
failure_reason: Chapter 11 after unsustainable land-grab pricing on genetic tests and $1.5B ArcherDX acquisition debt
lesson: Buying market share by pricing tests below cost only works if you find profitable adjacencies before the debt bill comes due. Invitae never did.

name: Cano Health
failure_reason: Chapter 11 after acquisition-led expansion left it with $1B+ debt and negative cash flow
lesson: Roll-up healthcare growth funded by debt is not "value-based care" — it is leverage waiting for a rate cycle to end it.

name: Nikola Corporation
failure_reason: Chapter 11 after years of fraud fallout, truck fires, and unsustainable cash burn on hydrogen infrastructure
lesson: Fraud at inception is a debt to reputation that keeps compounding. Even after Milton's conviction Nikola never recovered institutional trust.

name: Bowery Farming
failure_reason: Chapter 7 liquidation after vertical-farm unit economics never worked at scale
lesson: Growing lettuce indoors at grocery-shelf prices is a physics problem, not a software problem. Every VC-backed vertical farm has hit the same wall.

name: Plenty
failure_reason: Chapter 11 after strawberry pivot with Driscoll's failed to close unit-economics gap
lesson: Pivoting from lettuce to strawberries did not fix vertical-farming physics; it only bought Plenty one more round of runway.

name: Vroom
failure_reason: Wound down used-vehicle business after Carvana priced it out and unit economics collapsed
lesson: Being the #2 online used-car dealer during a rate cycle is the same as being dead. Vroom just took longer to realize it than the market.

name: Getir
failure_reason: Retreated from US, UK, Germany, Netherlands, Portugal, Spain, Italy in 2024 after 10-minute grocery model collapsed
lesson: Ten-minute grocery delivery is a marketing product that never generated ten-minute-grocery economics. The category compressed to zero in the West.

name: Bird Global
failure_reason: Chapter 11 after scooter unit economics, city permit costs and de-SPAC public listing destroyed the business
lesson: Being first in scooters was never a moat. Bird burned through nearly $900M proving that shared-scooter unit economics do not work at VC-required growth rates.

name: BeReal
failure_reason: Engagement collapse, no monetization, sold at fire-sale price
lesson: Viral hype is not a moat. A single-feature social app without monetization or daily engagement durability becomes worthless within 18 months.

name: Getir
failure_reason: Burnt cash on unit economics that never worked outside Turkey, ZIRP collapse
lesson: Hyper-local 10-minute delivery is a structurally unprofitable category outside dense, low-wage markets. Geographic expansion multiplied losses instead of revenue.

name: Maple
failure_reason: Negative unit economics on $12 meals with full vertical integration
lesson: Owning the kitchen, the food, the riders and the customer all at once gives you control but also concentrates every loss. Vertical integration is not a strategy in low-margin categories.

name: Jibo
failure_reason: Three-year shipping delay, $899 price point, undercut by Alexa and Google Home
lesson: Hardware timelines are unforgiving. If you take three years to ship, the market you launched into will not exist when you arrive.

name: Vine
failure_reason: Twitter neglect, failed to monetize creators, lost talent to Instagram and YouTube
lesson: Owning the creators is more important than owning the format. Vine invented short-form video and lost it because it never paid them.

name: Compass
failure_reason: Brokerage with software paint never earned tech multiples; 90%+ value destruction post-IPO
lesson: Calling yourself a tech company doesn't change your unit economics. Compass paid traditional brokerage commissions while spending tech-company money on software and recruiting.

name: Gorillas
failure_reason: Unprofitable dark-store model in Western Europe; absorbed by larger loss-maker
lesson: Being the fastest in a category with broken unit economics just gets you to bankruptcy first.

name: Sprig
failure_reason: Vertically integrated meal delivery at $12 price points lost money on every order
lesson: If your kitchen, your menu, your couriers and your app are all in-house, every single failure point is yours. In food delivery, that math doesn't work.

name: 23andMe
failure_reason: One-time DNA test had no recurring revenue; drug-discovery pivot failed; 2023 data breach destroyed trust
lesson: A consumer product without recurring revenue is not a business. 23andMe sold a one-time spit kit to 14M people and never figured out what to do next.

name: Essential Products
failure_reason: Late launch, weak reviews, founder scandal, Apple/Samsung/Chinese OEM lock on the premium segment
lesson: The premium Android segment is closed. A new entrant needs more than a famous founder and good industrial design — it needs distribution, ecosystem and a roadmap the competition can't beat.

name: Zulily
failure_reason: Flash-sales model lost to Amazon Prime; two waves of failure ending in liquidation
lesson: If your differentiator is 'cheaper than retail' in a world where Amazon is already cheaper than retail with two-day delivery, you don't have a business.

name: Honestbee
failure_reason: Unsustainable Unit Economics
lesson: Singapore's grocery-and-laundry on-demand pioneer expanded across SEA on $75M then ran out of cash with internal allegations of governance failures.

name: iPrice Group (Wind-Down)
failure_reason: Margin Compression & SEO Risk
lesson: SEA price-comparison aggregator iPrice raised US$25M then largely wound down as marketplaces (Lazada, Shopee) cut affiliate payouts.

name: Vouch (Wind-Down)
failure_reason: Post-COVID Demand & Margin
lesson: Singapore hotel-SaaS Vouch raised US$11M then wound down as Asian hotel-tech budgets failed to recover post-COVID.

name: Carousell (Down Round & Layoffs)
failure_reason: Path to Profitability Pressure
lesson: Singapore unicorn Carousell laid off 10% of staff and accepted flat/down rounds as classifieds margins remained elusive.

name: Mfine Singapore (Wind-Down)
failure_reason: Post-COVID Demand Collapse
lesson: Singapore-headquartered telehealth Mfine raised US$60M during COVID then heavily downsized as Asian telehealth demand normalized.

name: Vroom
failure_reason: Unit economics never worked online
lesson: Selling used cars fully online sounds like a Carvana copy — but without the reconditioning throughput, it's just an unprofitable middleman.

name: Casper Sleep
failure_reason: CAC caught up with LTV in a commodity category
lesson: A DTC 'lifestyle brand' becomes a mattress retailer the moment Facebook CPMs rise and 200 copycats appear.

name: Wag!
failure_reason: Two-sided marketplace beaten by Rover
lesson: SoftBank capital can subsidize demand, but not fix a marketplace losing to a better-loved incumbent.

name: Blue Apron
failure_reason: Rising CAC and churn in a commodity category
lesson: A subscription business only works when reactivation is cheaper than acquisition — meal kits proved neither.

name: Groupon
failure_reason: Daily-deals model was structurally deflationary
lesson: Selling merchants deep discounts trains customers to expect them and burns brand equity twice.

name: Hampton Creek / JUST
failure_reason: Governance scandal and mass board resignation
lesson: When the board resigns en masse, the story is not the product — it's the founder.

name: Made.com
failure_reason: Long lead times and inflation broke the model
lesson: A working-capital-intensive furniture business collapses instantly when shipping costs 5x and consumer demand halves.

name: Clinkle
failure_reason: Hype and founder drama with no shipping product
lesson: A record seed round is a liability if you can't ship — every month past launch date compounds distrust.

name: Jibo
failure_reason: Late shipment into a $199 Amazon Echo world
lesson: If your $899 product ships three years late into a category defined by a $199 competitor, the reviews don't save you.

name: OVO Mobile
failure_reason: MVNO margins can't survive UK price wars
lesson: Selling mobile plans as a UK MVNO means competing with EE, O2 and Sky at their marginal cost of a SIM — an unwinnable game.

name: Sidecar
failure_reason: Outspent by Uber and Lyft in the same city
lesson: Being first in a marketplace doesn't help if two better-funded competitors can subsidize both sides longer than you can.

name: WeWork
failure_reason: Overvaluation & Governance Failure
lesson: Confusing a real estate arbitrage business for a tech company enabled a $47B fantasy valuation that collapsed to bankruptcy in 4 years.

name: Theranos
failure_reason: Fraud & Technology That Never Worked
lesson: Silicon Valley 'fake it till you make it' collapses on contact with regulated healthcare — biological reality does not bend to press releases.

name: Quibi
failure_reason: No Product-Market Fit
lesson: Raising $1.75B before shipping guarantees you build the wrong product with no way to pivot.

name: Juicero
failure_reason: Solution In Search Of a Problem
lesson: A $400 WiFi-enabled press for juice packs you can squeeze by hand isn't innovation — it's the parody of Silicon Valley excess.

name: MoviePass
failure_reason: Unsustainable Unit Economics
lesson: Charging $9.95/month for a benefit that cost ~$40/month per user was not growth — it was subsidized customer acquisition at company-lethal scale.

name: Pets.com
failure_reason: Dot-Com Era Overexpansion
lesson: Selling 20lb bags of dog food below cost with free shipping in 1999 was less a business than a marketing budget with legs.

name: Webvan
failure_reason: Overexpansion Ahead of Demand
lesson: Building 26 automated warehouses before proving one worked is the textbook dot-com self-immolation.

name: Solyndra
failure_reason: Cost Curve Beat by Chinese Silicon
lesson: Betting a hardware startup on commodity prices staying high is a bet against manufacturing gravity — Chinese silicon PV crushed the math.

name: Jawbone
failure_reason: Outcompeted by Apple, Fitbit and Xiaomi
lesson: Raising $930M as a consumer hardware company chasing three losing categories (Bluetooth headsets, speakers, wearables) is a lesson in strategic drift.

name: Homejoy
failure_reason: Bad Unit Economics + Worker Misclassification
lesson: Subsidizing house cleaning at $19 introductory prices attracts one-time users, not a repeat customer base.

name: Beepi
failure_reason: Overspending + Poor Unit Economics
lesson: Renting a $1.5M office and paying employees Tesla lease bonuses before proving margins is how you incinerate $149M.

name: Munchery
failure_reason: Poor Unit Economics + Massive Food Waste
lesson: Cooking meals speculatively for hoped-for orders throws real food in the trash for hypothetical revenue.

name: Convoy
failure_reason: Freight Recession Killed Take Rates
lesson: Freight brokerage is a commodity margin business — a $3.8B valuation required a bull market that didn't come.

name: Fast
failure_reason: Revenue Miss + Founder Spending
lesson: A $124M-funded checkout startup with $600k annual revenue is a marketing budget with press releases.

name: Blockbuster
failure_reason: Disrupted by Netflix + Streaming
lesson: Turning down a $50M offer to buy Netflix in 2000 goes in the textbook next to Blockbuster's Chapter 11 filing.

name: Segway (2001-2020)
failure_reason: Hype vs Reality Gap
lesson: A product Steve Jobs said would 'reshape cities' at $5,000 apiece sold fewer units in a decade than iPhones do in a day.

name: Secret
failure_reason: Anonymity Turned Toxic Fast
lesson: An anonymous app that raised $25M with insiders selling secondary shares before the growth story broke — then burned out in 16 months.

name: The Messenger
failure_reason: Ad Revenue Miss + Executive Overhire
lesson: Jimmy Finkelstein's centrist news site raised $50M in 2023, hired 275 people, and closed 10 months later after ~$25M revenue.

name: Cue Health
failure_reason: Post-COVID Demand Collapse + FDA Warning
lesson: COVID-era demand for at-home testing masked a diagnostics business without a real everyday use case.

name: Brandless
failure_reason: Poor Repeat + High CAC
lesson: Selling everything for $3 doesn't scale a consumer packaged goods business — it just discounts the CAC into oblivion.

name: Scoot Networks
failure_reason: Unit Economics + Acquisition Whiplash
lesson: Bird acquired Scoot for $25M in 2019 and shuttered US operations 2020 amid COVID — completing the on-demand mobility collapse.

name: Better Place
failure_reason: Battery-Swap Model Failed
lesson: A $200,000-per-station battery-swap network needed EV volumes that Nissan Leaf and one Renault deal couldn't produce.

name: Nikola Motors
failure_reason: Founder Fraud + Product Delays
lesson: Trevor Milton's rolling-truck video demo turned into a securities fraud conviction and a company bankruptcy five years later.

name: Alikolo
failure_reason: Lack of vision and experience
lesson: Founders must maintain a clear vision, understand their competitive advantage, and retain sufficient ownership to steer the company's direction and secure future funding.

name: Aria Insights
failure_reason: Ahead of market demand, founder departure
lesson: Don't build solutions for problems that don't exist on a large enough scale for monetization, and be wary of significant strategic pivots.

name: ArsDigita
failure_reason: Inexperienced leadership, mismanagement, misguided product changes
lesson: Founders must maintain control and strategic vision, especially when bringing in external leadership, to avoid losing focus on core strengths and mismanaging resources.

name: BitPass
failure_reason: Unable to compete with free alternatives
lesson: Disruptive technology with a strong value proposition can quickly render established business models obsolete, especially when free alternatives emerge.

name: Call9
failure_reason: Unsustainable business model, rapid expansion
lesson: A novel business model requiring significant behavioral change in a regulated industry like healthcare, especially one that directly impacts physician compensation, faces immense uphill battles and requires robust financial planning.

name: Argyle Social
failure_reason: Intense competition, insufficient funding, API changes
lesson: Even with a good product, intense competition and external platform changes can quickly deplete resources and lead to failure without sufficient funding or effective adaptation.

name: Auctionata
failure_reason: Legal challenges, unethical practices, mismanagement
lesson: Ethical conduct and transparent management are crucial for long-term trust and investor confidence, as a lack thereof can lead to legal issues and ultimately, business failure.

name: 99dresses
failure_reason: Low revenue, technical debt, poor management
lesson: Early-stage startups need to ensure a viable business model from the start and prepare for necessary technical and management growth to sustain operations and scale effectively.

name: Circa
failure_reason: Lack of funds, unsustainable model
lesson: Even innovative news models struggle without a clear, sustainable revenue path, especially when giants can easily replicate and outcompete with established resources.

name: Crowdmix
failure_reason: Mismanagement of funds, lack of vision
lesson: Extravagant spending and lack of product focus can quickly deplete funds, even with significant investment.

name: Desti
failure_reason: Bad business model with poor revenue generation
lesson: Even innovative technology needs a strong, viable business model to generate revenue and survive against established competitors.

name: Design Inc.
failure_reason: Bad business model, market saturation
lesson: Focus on core business essentials, validate assumptions, and continuously optimize the product while fostering experimentation within the team.

name: Berg
failure_reason: No market need & high price
lesson: Even innovative products require a clear market need and a justifiable price point for sustained success.

name: Delicious
failure_reason: Acquisition Flu
